title: X Feed Digest
summary: Model upgrades and releases dominated the feed: Gemini 3 Deep Think hits Olympiad-level results while OpenAI ships GPT-5.3 Codex-Spark for low-latency coding and MiniMax M2.5 narrows the gap at far lower cost.
Agentic workflows are maturing: Claude Code customization + skills playbooks emphasize preconfigured agents and hooks, and Stripe’s x402 enables autonomous API payments.
AI infra economics stay front-and-center: Nebius shows demand outrunning GPU supply, while Goldman flags data-center power demand pushing electricity prices and inflation.
Usage scale keeps exploding, with OpenRouter reporting ~12T tokens/week—roughly Azure-scale inference.

items.title: @aakashgupta: Claude Code customization playbook
items.body: A detailed checklist of Claude Code knobs—model effort, permissions, hooks, and custom agents—with the key takeaway that preconfigured agents + lifecycle hooks unlock near-autonomous workflows.

items.title: @JeffDean: Gemini 3 Deep Think upgrade
items.body: Google says Gemini 3 Deep Think now hits Olympiad-level performance in physics/chemistry and posts SOTA results on ARC-AGI-2/MMMU-Pro/HLE, positioning it as a true research partner.

items.title: @dotey: GPT-5.3 Codex-Spark realtime model
items.body: OpenAI launched the low-latency Codex-Spark (Cerebras-backed) for interactive coding, highlighting faster response times and strong SWE/terminal benchmarks versus prior small models.

items.title: @runes_leo: Stripe adds x402 for agent payments
items.body: Stripe integrated x402 so agents can pay APIs in USDC when servers return HTTP 402, enabling autonomous pay-per-call without human checkout flows.

items.title: @bridgemindai: MiniMax M2.5 price/perf leap
items.body: BridgeBench shows MiniMax M2.5 within 0.4 points of Opus 4.6 but ~8× cheaper, suggesting Chinese labs are winning on price-performance.

items.title: @deedydas: OpenRouter usage scale
items.body: OpenRouter token consumption reportedly jumped 12.7× YoY to ~12.1T tokens/week—about as much inference as all of Azure, signaling massive demand growth.

items.title: @ReyezAriel: Nebius earnings highlight AI cloud demand
items.body: Nebius posted Q4 revenue of $228M (+547%) and ARR of $1.2B, with capacity sold out into 2026; guidance and capex point to demand far outpacing GPU supply despite near-term revenue timing issues.

items.title: @fxtrader: Datacenter power demand pressure
items.body: Goldman says data-center electricity demand is driving power prices up ~6.9% YoY and could add ~0.2/0.15 pts to PCE inflation in 2026/2027, with heavier impact on low-income households.

items.title: @KKaWSB: ByteDance Seedance 2.0 market shock
items.body: Commentary notes Seedance 2.0’s viral launch rattled markets (Kuaishou down, HSTECH volatility) and argues ByteDance’s full-stack AI push is rewriting competitive moats across ads, ecommerce, and content.

items.title: @immersivetran: The productivity power of “No”
items.body: A summary of James Clear’s essay arguing the highest-leverage productivity move is refusing commitments early, preserving time for the few things that matter most.

items.title: @waitbutwhy: X’s fake-news phase shift
items.body: Argues X has moved into an era where fabricated stories dominate; calls for algorithmic penalties for scammers because Community Notes/Grok lag behind viral spread.
